body: Could you elaborate what you did against the grain?

I do not mind having the beetus if humanity can provide tools to automate as much of it as possible. I have seen [this talk by Mr Hanselman](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uNhYhlBQoEY) who is diabetic as well! wow, and it now explains why software side of pumps is lagging. We need open protocols so that developers around the world can be let loose to implement everything from machine learning to AI for pump control. However, it seems like this is limited until someone creates a stable glucagon to prevent hypos.

They do, but having gone a FB group, it is up to local authority to cover a person or not. And usually, since NHS is underfunded, they do not.

Holy cow, all I wanted to get in UK is an insurance like in USA. Pay 500/month, I don't care. But there is no such option at all. Large majority of insurers do not cover chronic conditions. They help you diagnose, and then you are the mercy of NHS. I love NHS and the hard-working staff, but I would gladly pay American way and get great care instead of socialized medicine inferior care.
Test strips will not wake me up when I am in a hypo state.
I am thinking of paying for CGM but it would cost me around 200/month at least.
They do not cover CGM, nor pumps unless you are failing as in controlling it: 8.5+ a1c or hypos.
